text:
Friends and fans of Molly Meldrum have remembered the music industry great, who died Monday at the age of 83.
Meldrum spent more than a decade hosting ABC music show Countdown, leaving a lasting legacy on the Australian music landscape.
Jason Donovan said Meldrum was the “very heart” of the music program while he was growing up, calling the man a “truly unique character, a great Australian and one of this country’s greatest pioneers and ambassadors for music and entertainment”.
“He was loved, recognised and respected around the world for the extraordinary contribution he made to Australian music and the artists he championed,” Donovan wrote on Facebook. “There will never be another quite like him.”
The former Neighbors star shared a memory of Meldrum appearing on an episode alongside Kylie Minogue and Guy Pearce, adding: “what a day that was!”
Gavin Wood, a longtime friend of Meldrum’s who worked on Countdown, said the man was “one of the craziest, most colourful, funniest and most beautiful people you could ever have the pleasure of meeting”.
“What he has done for the Australian music industry is simply phenomenal,” Wood wrote. “His contribution, passion, enthusiasm and unwavering commitment to Australian artists helped shape an entire generation of music and entertainment.
“There will never be another Molly Meldrum. You simply cannot measure anyone against him.”
Bands and artists echoed those sentiments.
“He was such a huge presence in the Australian music industry and was a great friend and supporter of so many up and coming bands and artists – ourselves included,” the band Human Nature wrote. “Thanks for everything Molly. Rest easy.”
The St Kilda football club remembered Meldrum as a “lifelong Sainter”, saying the organisation was deeply saddened by his death.
“An iconic and passionate supporter of our football club, Molly changed and brightened the lives of so many across a storied career,” the club wrote on Facebook.
The immigration minister, Tony Burke, said that Australia had lost an icon.
“For generations of Australians, Molly was more than a familiar face on our television screens,” Burke wrote. “He was an advocate of Australian music, talent scout, journalist, producer and broadcaster who helped shape the soundtrack of our nation.”
Mark Klemens, Meldrum’s friend and longtime manager, said the “true Australian icon” had “opened doors for so many and entertained millions”.
“He was unconventional and wonderfully unpredictable, but always caring, always funny and always down to earth, with a passion the rest of us could only envy,” Klemens said. “He made the most of his life, and boy, was it a full one.”

עולם המוזיקה באוסטרליה ומחוצה לה נפרד ממולי מელדרום, מנחה תוכנית המוזיקה המיתולוגית Countdown ואיש ע스티ות מרכזי שהלך לעולמו בגיל 83. מელדרום זכה להערכה רבה בזכות תרומתו העצומה למוזיקה האוסטרלית ולקידום אמנים לאורך עשרות שנים.

דמויות בולטות, בהן ג'ייסון דונובן, להקת Human Nature ומועדון הכדורגל סנט קילדה, העלו זיכרונות וציינו את תרומתו הייחודית ואישיותו הצבעונית. שר ההגירה האוסטרלי טוני ברק וגורמים נוספים הדגישו את היותו סמל תרבות ודמות משמעותית שעיצבה את התרבות המקומית.
